For fields with reduced Compton wavelengths no shorter than the black-hole mass scale, the numerical errors in the frequency shifts are typically $10^{-8} - 10^{-5}$ for dimensionless spins between 0 and 0.9, and at most $\mathcal{O}(10^{-3})$ next to the scalar-mass threshold. Our results open up the possibility of searching for ultralight scalar particles, prime dark-matter candidates, using existing gravitational-wave signals.

entries.title: WALLABY pilot survey: accurate and automated linewidth measurements from global HI profiles
entries.abstract: Current-generation 21-cm surveys of extragalactic neutral hydrogen (HI) with instruments such as FAST and ASKAP are providing detailed spectral and spatial information for over 10^5 galaxies. Future HI surveys with next-generation radio telescopes could provide sample sizes larger by orders of magnitude. There is therefore a need for accurate, automated, and reliable parameterisation of the HI emission from galaxies. We have developed an automated estimator for HI global profile widths to better enable studies of, for example, dynamical masses and Tully-Fisher distances. Our estimator is based on an implementation of the BusyFit profile-fitting algorithm, and converges for 95% of global profiles in the WALLABY pilot survey. Probability density functions are calculated for all profile parameters using Monte Carlo techniques, and example error parameterisations are given. We confirm that linewidth uncertainties depend primarily on the integrated signal-to-noise ratio, profile steepness, and the linewidth, consistent with previous studies. We compare several common linewidth definitions, and the width at 50% of the mean flux density (Wm50) is found to be the most robust measure of linewidth. We provide examples of the baryonic Tully-Fisher relation drawn from the WALLABY pilot survey.

entries.title: Radiation-Regulated Spherical Accretion with an Inner Accretion Disk
entries.abstract: We develop a theoretical model for radiation-regulated spherical accretion with an inner accretion disk. In our model, the outer accretion flow remains quasi-spherical and optically thick, while the luminosity generated by the inner disk is self-consistently coupled to the accretion rate and irradiates the inflowing gas. By solving the global transonic structure with radiative transfer treated in the diffusion approximation, we investigate how radiation regulates the flow structure and the accretion rate. We find that the luminosity is constrained by a generalized Eddington limit, leading to a saturated accretion rate typically lower than the classical Bondi prediction by orders of magnitude. At sufficiently low densities, the enthalpy flux of the spherical inflow contributes substantially to the emergent luminosity, in which case the inner disk luminosity is reduced and the accretion flow enters an unsaturated state. A criterion is derived to estimate whether the accretion flow is saturated. We further demonstrate the applicability of our model by considering fallback accretion in failed supernova systems. The predicted nearly constant emergent luminosity, constrained by the generalized Eddington limit, provides a possible explanation for the observed luminosity plateau in the failed supernova candidate M31-2014-DS1. The presence of an inner disk also provides sufficient radiation to avoid the under-luminous predictions of a purely spherical fallback model extending down to the central object. Our model provides a framework for studying radiation-regulated accretion flows in systems where low but finite angular momentum leads to the formation of an accretion disk within a larger-scale quasi-spherical inflow.

entries.title: Equation of State Classification of Core-Collapse Supernovae with a Network of Gravitational-Wave Detectors
entries.abstract: Gravitational waves from core-collapse supernovae may provide a unique probe of the equation of state (EOS) of dense nuclear matter. In previous work, we assessed the potential of machine-learning methods for EOS classification for rapidly rotating supernovae using individual gravitational-wave detectors. Here, we extend the framework to detector networks and investigate the impact of detector configuration, source distance, arrival time, and sky location on the classification. Using convolutional neural networks, we perform 10-class EOS classification directly from noisy detector data for both second- and third-generation observatories. We find that detector geometry strongly influences classification performance. For Galactic events, current detector networks can achieve promising classification performance, but the reach depends sensitively on the detector network antenna response. Adding detectors improves time-averaged performance and produces more uniform classification across the sky. Third-generation observatories extend the classification reach to 100 kpc for favorable source orientations but do not remove the dependence on detector geometry.

entries.title: Intrinsic Soft X-ray Emission from the Hot Circumgalactic Medium in IllustrisTNG
entries.abstract: We study the intrinsic 0.5--2~keV emission of the hot circumgalactic medium (CGM) in the IllustrisTNG simulation TNG100-2 at redshifts 0, 0.1, and 0.2. We calculate the emission of gas cells with $T \geq 10^6$~K in the spherical shell between $0.15R_{500}$ and $R_{500}$ and compare samples selected by their star-formation activity. X-ray luminosity increases with halo mass, although the class-dependent fits cover different mass intervals. Among galaxies with positive luminosity and star formation rate (SFR), the high-activity sample retains a positive association after a linear adjustment for halo mass. The residual association is weaker in the quiescent subset with positive luminosity and SFR. Within $10^{11.75}<M_{500}/M_\odot<10^{12.25}$, the high-activity sample has more centrally concentrated emission and a median luminosity about five times that of the quiescent sample. The two populations have similar median hot-gas masses despite their different X-ray luminosities and radial profiles. These differences are consistent with variations in the spatial distribution and thermodynamic state of the emitting gas, although the samples are not matched in halo mass. Our results suggest that soft X-ray emission probes the structure of the hot CGM as well as its gas content, offering a way to investigate how star formation and feedback shape gaseous halos.

entries.title: Galaxy Clusters from the DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys. IV. Alignment of Member Galaxy Orientations at z < 0.5
entries.abstract: Using DESI photometric catalog data, we systematically analyze the spatial alignment of star-forming galaxies (SFGs) and quiescent galaxies (QGs) in clusters. The results reveal that, in both brightest central galaxy (BCG) alignment (BA) and satellite alignment (SA), the alignment signals of SFGs and QGs exhibit opposite trends in several aspects. For the BA signal, SFGs show stronger alignment in cluster outskirts, whereas QGs exhibit stronger alignment in inner regions. For the SA signal, both SFGs and QGs exhibit nearly isotropic signals in outer regions, while in inner regions they show opposite signals. In addition, the BA signal depends on cluster richness and QG fraction, and is more pronounced in mature clusters. Specifically, QGs show a stronger BA signal overall, which increases with luminosity and axis ratio, whereas SFGs show a weaker BA signal with no significant dependence on these parameters. The BA signal also exhibits a strong dependence on satellite galaxy color, which is independent of morphology. We confirm this by analyzing the BA signal in two populations: red disk and blue elliptical galaxies. However, neither BA nor SA shows a significant dependence on redshift at z < 0.5. In summary, these findings reflect how galaxy transport along cosmic filaments drives cluster evolution: early-stage SFGs fall into clusters along filaments, and during cluster relaxation, their spatial orientations are reshaped by gravitational potentials and tidal forces, weakening BA signal and enhancing SA signal. In contrast, QGs, as early cluster members, exhibit a more pronounced anisotropic distribution and maintain relatively stable spatial orientations.

entries.title: Deep learning methods for gamma event selection in TAIGA-IACT image analysis in stereo-mode
entries.abstract: In astrophysical complex TAIGA there are four Imaging Atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes (IACTs), located at a distance of 300-500 m from each other, due to which extensive air showers (EAS) generated by cosmic and gamma radiation are recorded by a single telescope or by multiple telescopes simultaneously (stereo-mode). The analysis of EAS images from two or more Cherenkov telescopes together is of particular interest, since for this approach the reconstruction of physical parameters of the primary gamma ray is much more accurate than in mono-observations. However, the gamma-ray event reconstruction strongly depends on the quality of the hadron background suppression of the classifier, therefore, the gamma event selection stage is one of the important ones in the further analysis of IACT data. We propose and study several neural network methods for gamma event selection in joint TAIGA-IACT image analysis. Neural network methods we suggested involves a single-stage analysis of IACT images from two telescopes, while the second method considers the formation of autoencoder-derived essential features that contain the EAS physical parameters, including the type of primary particle.

entries.title: Direct Observational Constraint on Upstream Magnetic Field Amplification Reveals the Particle Acceleration Limit in a Supernova Remnant
entries.abstract: The origin of Galactic cosmic rays up to the knee energy (PeV) remains a long-standing open question in astrophysics. Supernova remnant shocks are leading candidates for accelerating particles to PeV energies, yet this requires strong magnetic field amplification in the upstream region to confine the highest energy particles. Despite its importance, the upstream magnetic field strength has long lacked direct observational constraints. Here we report the observation of numerous synchrotron X-ray hotspots extending into the upstream of the supernova remnant RX J1713.7$-$3946 in archival Chandra data. These hotspots show spatial and temporal properties consistent with synchrotron emission from secondary electrons produced by hadronic interactions between accelerated protons and dense molecular clumps. Using the spatial extent of these upstream hotspots as a physical scale, we estimate the proton diffusion length to be $\sim 1~\mathrm{pc}$. This measurement provides a constraint on the upstream magnetic field strength of $\sim 10~μ\mathrm{G}$, which is consistent with recent simulations of Bell-instability-driven magnetic field amplification. Our results indicate that the current amplification is insufficient to reach PeV energies, explaining the observed TeV gamma-ray spectral cutoff and providing a diagnostic for assessing PeVatron capability in stellar shocks.

entries.title: Grand minima and intermittency in near-critical convection-driven dynamos
entries.abstract: Context: Solar magnetism exhibits long-term variations on timescales of decades to centuries. Aims: The main aim is to study how the supercriticality of the dynamo affects the variability of magnetic fields on timescales relevant to the Sun. Methods: Three-dimensional rotating magnetohydrodynamic simulations in a spherical wedge geometry are used to produce self-consistent convection-driven dynamos. The supercriticality of the dynamo is controlled by varying the magnetic diffusivity. Results: The main result is that long-term variability of the dynamo increases with decreasing supercriticality of the dynamo and that cases nearest to the onset of dynamo action show extended grand minima-like periods of low activity. The simulations fall in three classes where the least supercritical cases show the largest variations of magnetic activity and where the flow including differential rotation is almost unaffected by the magnetic field. In the cases with the highest supercriticality the magnetic field is permanently strong and differential rotation permanently quenched, both having relatively little temporal variation. In an intermediate regime both the magnetic fields and differential rotation exhibit strong anticorrelated fluctuations. Conclusions: The occurrence of grand minima in the Sun has been conjectured to be due to a weakly supercritical dynamo. The current results support this idea and suggest that the absence of grand minima in earlier global dynamo simulations is because their large-scale dynamos were too supercritical. Furthermore, the current results suggest that the effect of the magnetic field on differential rotation is negligible if the average rms-field is less than about 2~kG.

entries.title: Unveiling photometric transients with the ILMT and their follow-up using DOT
entries.abstract: The two 4-m class telescopes at the Devasthal site in India are complementary: the 4-m International Liquid Mirror Telescope (ILMT) is dedicated to the discovery of new transient phenomena, which can be followed up using the 3.6-m Devasthal Optical Telescope (DOT) for their optical characterisation. The ILMT continuously surveys a $22.3^\prime \times 22.3^\prime$ wide strip of the zenith sky. A dedicated transient detection and classification pipeline, PyLMT, based on optimised image subtraction and convolutional neural network (CNN) techniques, enables the discovery of numerous photometric transients with the ILMT. However, these transient discoveries still require spectroscopic confirmation to determine their types, for which spectra obtained with the DOT are essential. Here, we present a selection of photometric transients, specifically supernova candidates. We investigate their photometric and spectroscopic properties using ILMT light curves, supplemented with ZTF data and DOT spectroscopic observations.

entries.title: From the QBO to Rieger-type periods: Explaining extreme solar events by tidally triggered magneto-Rossby waves
entries.abstract: It has recently been demonstrated that the occurrence of extreme solar events is governed by a phase-stable period close to 1.723 years (629.29 days). According to our previously developed tidally-synchronized solar dynamo model, this is one of the periods resulting from two-planet spring tides exerted by the tidally dominant planets Venus, Earth and Jupiter, which trigger magneto-Rossby waves in the solar tachocline. Overall, the squared sum of these three waves incorporates nine periods ranging from 59 to 629 days. Using a standard Rayleigh test, we demonstrate that all nine of these periods can be identified in the data on extreme solar events. For the latter, we use a combination of 72 ground-level enhancement (GLE) events with various X-flare data, the number of which increases when the threshold is successively lowered from X10 to X1. To identify the spectral peaks, it is necessary to analyze the sidebands that emerge due to the modulation with the longer-term periods such as the 11-year Schwabe cycle and the third harmonics of the Hale cycle. In this framework, the seminal Rieger period of 154 days is re-interpreted as the lower sideband of 146 days which is the quarter of the synodic period of Venus and Earth.

entries.title: SiO Maser Line-width Diagnostics of AGB Stars and Red Supergiants: The RSG-adjacent Region in the FWZI--Luminosity Plane
entries.abstract: We investigate whether SiO maser line profiles can distinguish asymptotic giant branch (AGB) stars from red supergiants (RSGs) and identify unusual AGB-classified sources near the RSG regime. We compiled 2,956 detected SiO maser spectra for 1,551 objects and constructed reference samples of 1,068 O-rich AGB stars and 36 RSGs. The full width at zero intensity (FWZI) was reliably measured for 1,020 AGB stars and 32 RSGs. AGB stars are concentrated at narrow line widths: 81.5% have FWZI <10 km s^-1, whereas 81.2% of RSGs have FWZI >15 km s^-1 and none has FWZI <10 km s^-1. Infrared two-color diagrams provide only partial separation. Combining FWZI with luminosities based primarily on quality-filtered Gaia/Bailer-Jones distances, with independent literature distances for several RSGs, reveals a weak tendency for wider SiO maser lines at higher luminosities but no clean boundary. We therefore define an empirical RSG-adjacent region in the FWZI-luminosity plane, 15 <= FWZI <= 26.6 km s^-1 and 3.9 <= log(L/L_sun) <= 4.9, to characterize the high-luminosity, broad-line tail of the AGB-classified sample. Ten sources fall within this region. Using infrared SEDs, DUSTY fits, OH/H2O maser information, and variability, we find that six are most naturally interpreted as luminous AGB-like objects, two warrant follow-up to assess possible high-initial-mass AGB, RSG-like, or SAGB-related interpretations, and two are less securely constrained because of poor DUSTY fits. The RSG-adjacent region is therefore a physically mixed screening space, not a definitive classification box, for selecting high-priority follow-up targets.

entries.title: Nearly pristine gas in a galaxy 1 billion years after the Big Bang
entries.abstract: Excitation of carbon and oxygen ions is the primary mechanism by which collapsing gas clouds dissipate heat to form new stars. At early cosmic times, in galaxies with chemically pristine gas, many stars are expected to have masses far larger than the mass of our sun due to the deficit in these elements. We searched for ultra-metal-poor galaxies using their spectroscopic absorption signatures in front of bright background quasars, employing the new GHOST high-resolution spectrograph. Here we report the discovery of the first galaxy containing a reservoir of neutral hydrogen gas with metallicity below the ultra-metal-poor threshold: with a measured carbon-to-hydrogen ratio 11,000 times lower than the Sun, it is the most pristine ever found by a factor of four. UMP-DLA-1 is the only known galaxy with measured carbon and oxygen abundances too low to enable efficient formation of stars with solar mass or below. The low metallicity alone therefore guarantees a top-heavy stellar population, providing a direct view of the chemical composition imprinted by massive low-metallicity stars that perished long before the present day: an elevated oxygen-to-carbon ratio. The abundance pattern of UMP-DLA-1 is likely a close representation of the atomic yields of first- or early second-generation stars.

entries.title: Blackbody evolution and circumstellar medium properties of broad-lined H-rich superluminous supernovae
entries.abstract: Broad-lined H-rich superluminous supernovae (SLSNe II) tend to show signs of interaction, including a UV excess compared to a blackbody function. However, a quantitative analysis of the CSM configuration and the UV excess has so far not been performed for most of the literature sample. Additionally, SN 2023gpw showed signs of asymmetry in its peculiar blackbody and spectral evolution, raising the question of whether similar properties can be found in other SLSNe II. We aim to characterize the circumstellar environment of SLSNe II by searching for signs of asymmetry, quantifying the UV excess, and investigating any IR echoes produced by dust. Diversity among SLSNe II is also explored. We fit blackbody functions to the SEDs of SLSNe II to quantify the UV excess luminosity and its evolution. We use this to investigate mass-loss rates required to produce the excess through interaction. We also investigate the line profiles in SLSN II at late times and compare line velocities to the blackbody radius evolution. We examine public WISE IR images and place constraints on IR echoes. We find mass loss rates of $\sim10^{-4}$ to $\sim0.03\, \mathrm{M_\odot}$~yr$^{-1}$ when assuming all interaction luminosity emerges in the UV, i.e., conservative lower limits for the total mass loss rate. Radii calculated from line velocities in late-time spectra are mostly too large for a spherical interaction photosphere, only compatible with the blackbody radius evolution if the CSM is non-spherical with a low filling factor. This is in some cases supported by a mismatch between spectroscopic and blackbody expansion velocities. Considerable diversity is seen in the sample, probably as a result of different viewing angles and CSM masses. WISE images seem too shallow to observe IR echoes in SLSNe II beyond $z\sim0.1$, but in the nearest event, SN 2020jhm, a likely IR echo is detected, suggesting pre-existing dust.

entries.title: Aditya-L1 and SDO Observations of a Confined X-Class Flare with an EUV Late Phase: Thermal and Nonthermal Emission, Magnetic Topology, and Flux Rope Confinement
entries.abstract: We study a long-duration, confined X2.0-class solar flare exhibiting three distinct episodes of HXR emission, along with an accompanying EUV late phase. A key highlight of this work is the novel observations from the high-resolution solar X-ray spectrometers SoLEXS and HEL1OS onboard Aditya-L1, providing insights into the evolution of thermal and non-thermal emissions. Simultaneous EUV observations from AIA/SDO in hot channels, combined with multi-band X-ray light curves, reveal a two-stage confined eruption of a large MFR, separated by $\sim$10~minutes. The first stage corresponds to an M4.6 flare, while the overall event reaches X2.0 on the GOES scale. During the first phase, magnetic reconnection beneath the large EUV hot channel causes plasma heating to $\sim$19~MK, with a non-thermal spectral index of $\sim$4.3. In the second phase, characterized by external reconnection and confinement of the MFR hot channel, the temperature increases to $\sim$22~MK, accompanied by further hardening of the spectral index to $\sim$3.9. Despite pronounced non-thermal signatures and enhanced particle acceleration, the MFR fails to erupt through the overlying coronal loops because of the strong strapping force exerted by the large overlying coronal loops. Importantly, the stalled eruption, together with reconnection in the higher overlying loops, results in enhanced heating within a closed magnetic configuration, with temperatures peaking at up to $\sim$15~MK during the late phase. The paper also provides the first observations of detectable non-thermal X-ray emission during the early EUV late phase, albeit briefly, providing direct evidence for reconnection-induced heating, likely occurring in the higher overlying coronal loops.

entries.title: Identifying the principal mechanism of star formation feedback
entries.abstract: Feedback from massive stars regulates the formation of next-generation stars and planets and thus shapes the evolution of galaxies, yet observational evidence capable of determining which mechanism dominates the feedback process has long been lacking. Here,we present a large-scale HI survey toward Orion A$.$ With an unprecedented sensitivity and superior resolution, FAST (Five-hundred-meter Aperture Spherical radio Telescope) reveals a well-defined heart-shaped expanding HI bubble, enshrouding the well-known "Veil" bubble of ionized gas. The photoionization-driven and wind-driven gas expands at 10.9 and 13.8 kilometers per second, respectively, with a kinetic energy ratio of 1:2 assuming a spherical symmetry and a uniform HI-to-H2 ratio. This first direct comparison within a single bubble shows that radiation does not dominate the feedback process as predicted by classical theories; instead, stellar winds contribute a comparable share of the injected kinetic energy.

entries.title: The Thousand-Pulsar-Array programme on MeerKAT - XX. Co-existing interacting periodicities and polarization modulation in PSR J1901-0906
entries.abstract: We present a comprehensive analysis of the complex subpulse modulation in PSR J1901-0906 using data from the Thousand-Pulsar-Array (TPA) programme. Our analysis reveals the coexistence of three distinct periodicities in the subpulse modulation of both profile components, which obey a beat relation. We also detect additional spectral beat features caused by the modulation of these co-existing periodicities by investigating the Fourier phase correlation in two-dimensional fluctuation spectra. Moreover, the single-pulse polarization states are shown to be modulated and synchronized with the three co-existing periodicities observed in total intensity. Such synchronization has been reported for only a small number of pulsars, but this discovery marks the only one where this synchronization involves multiple co-existing periodicities. The modulation beats are similar to, yet more complex than, the beat system previously identified in PSR J1514-4834 with higher-order harmonics playing a significant role. The coexistence of the observed beat-like periodicities in PSR J1901-0906 implies that they are not independent, but rather originate from an underlying, interconnected physical system within the pulsar magnetosphere. Building upon the same geometric framework previously applied to PSR J1514-4834, we demonstrate that a feedback system with interacting rotating carousels successfully reproduces the complex subpulse modulations observed in PSR J1901-0906 and naturally explains the beat relations.

entries.title: An Intermediate-orbit Brown Dwarf Confirmed with Astrometry+Radial Velocity Joint Analysis, and the Eccentricity Distribution of Brown Dwarfs Across Different Locations
entries.abstract: Intermediate-orbit ($\sim 1$ AU) brown dwarfs with absolute mass measurements are essential for understanding the evolution of substellar objects. Although such systems remain rare, their number is now being enlarged thanks to astrometry. Here, we present the absolute mass measurements for HD 203771B, a massive brown dwarf orbiting a K dwarf ($M_\ast=0.79\pm0.08\ M_\odot$) with a period of 1140 days on an eccentric ($e\approx0.5$) and inclined ($i\approx 130^{\circ}$) orbit. Through joint analysis of (1) radial velocities and Gaia two-body solution, as well as (2) radial velocities, Hipparcos Intermediate Astrometric Data and two-epoch Gaia astrometry, we obtain true companion masses of $74.20^{+3.46}_{-3.64} M_{\mathrm{J}}$ and $69.03^{+4.99}_{-4.95} M_{\mathrm{J}}$, respectively, agreeing with each other within $1σ$. Taking a sample of 159 brown dwarfs with absolute mass measurements from different detection techniques, we investigate their eccentricity distributions across different semi-major axis ranges by fitting a Beta distribution. We find that the peak of eccentricity distribution tends to gradually shift toward lower values from wide orbits ($a>20$ AU) to intermediate ($1<a<20$ AU) and inner ($0.1<a<1$ AU) regions. Such trend is plausibly due to disk friction during orbital evolution. Together with obliquity studies showing that brown dwarfs are mostly aligned, our result suggests that brown dwarfs may migrate inward through quiescent coplanar disk-driven processes.

entries.title: Environmental Dependence of Satellite Planarity and Orbital-Pole Coherence around Milky Way Analogues in a Hydrodynamical Cosmological Simulation
entries.abstract: We examine whether the unusual spatial flattening and orbital-plane coherence of the Milky Way's classical satellites are connected to the Galaxy's location in the cosmic web. We compare the 11 classical satellites with the 11 most massive satellites of 11,922 Milky Way-mass hosts in the TNG300-1 hydrodynamical simulation. We measure flattening with both the simple inertia tensor (SIT), which retains radial information, and the reduced inertia tensor (RIT), which isolates angular anisotropy. Orbital-plane coherence is characterized by the minimum opening angle containing the axes of the eight most coplanar satellite orbits. For the Milky Way, we find $(c/a,b/a)=(0.183,0.558)$ for SIT and $(0.364,0.736)$ for RIT, together with an eight-orbit opening angle of $21.9^\circ$. The corresponding fractions of simulated systems at least as extreme are $4.94\%$, $12.28\%$, and $5.04\%$, respectively. We describe the environment using the velocity-shear tensor smoothed on $2\,h^{-1}\mathrm{Mpc}$ and compare the full sample with Local Group-like pairs, systems whose shear eigenvalues match those reconstructed for the Local Group, and hosts in knots, filaments, sheets, and voids. Among the well-sampled environmental subsets, the shape and opening-angle distributions differ only weakly. Although the cosmic web imprints preferred orientations on host spins and satellite orbital-plane axes, the Milky Way combines orientations that are uncommon in the simulation. We conclude that the present-day cosmic-web environment alone does not substantially increase the occurrence of Milky Way-like satellite configurations. This result does not rule out an origin in anisotropic accretion, since neither the present-day web class nor its shear eigenvalues fully encodes the assembly history of an individual satellite system.

entries.title: TESS flares and chromospheric variability in the Pleiades, the Hyades, and Praesepe
entries.abstract: Magnetic activity is a result of the interaction between rotation and dynamo processes in cool stars with outer convection zones. Since open cluster members share a common age, distance, and chemical composition, they provide an opportunity to study the magnetic activity of cool stars in a controlled astrophysical context. We used 120s cadence observations from the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) to study the flare activity of stars in three open clusters with different ages: the Pleiades (100 Myr), the Hyades (700 Myr) and Praesepe (700 Myr). We used the Ohio State Multi-Object Spectrograph (OSMOS) at MDM Observatory with the goal of identifying coronal mass ejections (CMEs) in the Pleiades and Praesepe. We investigated the flaring characteristics of the cluster members using the TESS light curves: we identified the flares, then divided the dataset into different categories based on the effective temperature and light curve amplitude. We calculated the flare energies and investigated the flare frequency distributions. We studied the dynamic spectra of the H$α$ line and its environment to search for indication of CMEs. The power-law indices of the flare frequency distributions obtained in our analysis span the 1.8-2.8 range. We found the highest flare rates in the Pleiades for all investigated spectral types. Our results show that the flare rate of M dwarfs is similar in the Pleiades and the Hyades while for K-type stars the flare rate in the Pleiades is an order of magnitude higher. Our analysis reveals that the flare rate in M stars changes with their effective temperature: the rate is highest for T$_{eff}$ $\sim$3200-3300 K -coinciding with the transition between partially and fully convective stars - with smooth decrease in flare rate towards cooler and hotter M dwarfs. We used the MDM/OSMOS spectra to place an upper limit on the CME rate.

entries.title: Evidence for Hierarchical Turbulent Scaling in Nearby Star-Forming Galaxies
entries.abstract: We find recurring signatures of intermittency in molecular-gas velocities from cloud to galactic scales. In 31 selected galaxies from PHANGS-ALMA, velocity-centroid exponents through sixth order show nonlinear order dependence and nearly linear relations between consecutive exponents across galaxies. Positive estimated offsets from single-exponent scaling occur in all 52 galaxies with a valid power law fit and 99 of 100 clouds. A generalized She-Leveque hierarchy accommodates these signatures, supporting a hierarchical description of turbulent scaling in molecular gas across these environments.

entries.title: Double Detonations on a Moving Mesh with $\texttt{Cattails}$: Characterizing Early Reddening in SNe Ia
entries.abstract: Type Ia supernovae are useful as cosmological distance indicators and are significant sources of chemical enrichment in galaxies, but much about their origins remains uncertain. The double detonation explosion mechanism is one promising model for these transients. We present a suite of thermonuclear hydrodynamic double detonation models of sub-Chandrasekhar mass white dwarfs spanning thin to thick helium shells. Thin shell models produce light curves and spectra consistent with normal Type Ia supernovae, and thicker shell models have early time luminosity bumps from radioactive ashes in the shell and early reddening in color sometimes observed in peculiar Type I supernovae. The reddening is due to line blanketing from heavy elements produced in the shell detonation encompassing the central emission. We perform the computations using $\texttt{Cattails}$, a moving mesh nuclear hydrodynamics code introduced in this work. After carrying out subsequent radiative transfer calculations using the $\texttt{Sedona}$ code, we relate the time of early reddening to the mass of the initial helium shell. We also consider how the relation changes as a function of total mass as well as how the peak brightness depends on the total mass. Finally, we provide a series of fitting functions that can be used to estimate the mass of the shell consistent with an observation of reddening in the early color evolution of a type Ia supernova.

entries.title: Unveiling the Hot Interstellar Medium in Nearby Galaxies with eROSITA
entries.abstract: Diffuse X-ray emission in galaxies originates from stellar-feedback-heated gas and unresolved compact sources. We investigate its thermal component and the scaling of X-ray luminosity with star formation rate (SFR), including galaxies with very low SFRs. We analyzed eROSITA/SRG data from the four all-sky surveys (eRASS:4) for a blind, volume-limited sample of 140 galaxies within 25 Mpc from the Updated Nearby Galaxy Catalog (Karachentsev et al. 2013), cross-matched with HECATEv2 (Kyritsis et al. 2026b). Early-type galaxies were analyzed separately, while star-forming galaxies were divided into low-, medium-, and high-specific-SFR (sSFR) subsamples. We modeled the integrated X-ray spectra with thermal plasma and power-law components, stacked spectra for each subsample, and derived total and thermal X-ray luminosities. The stacked spectra show a stronger soft thermal component at high sSFR, whereas low-sSFR and early-type galaxies are increasingly dominated by the harder non-thermal continuum. For star-forming galaxies, the total 0.5-8 keV luminosity follows $\log L_X \sim 39.5 + 0.9\log\mathrm{SFR}$, with an intrinsic scatter of about 0.9 dex. The 0.5-2 keV thermal luminosity follows $\log L_X \sim 38.7 + 1.1\log\mathrm{SFR}$, with an intrinsic scatter of about 0.7 dex. The thermal luminosity remains well correlated with SFR down to $\sim 10^{-5}\,\mathrm{M}_\odot\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$ and is consistent with previous relations for star-forming galaxies. By contrast, the flatter and more scattered total X-ray luminosity-SFR relation suggests that unresolved X-ray binaries likely dominate at low SFR, while thermal X-ray emission remains a robust tracer of stellar feedback.

entries.title: Self-Interacting Dark Matter: From Particle Physics Theories to Structure Formation Simulations
entries.abstract: We present a unified theory-to-simulation framework for self-interacting dark matter (SIDM), combining a self-contained introduction to its particle-physics foundations and representative benchmark models with an explicit, systematic mapping to simulation inputs and validated numerical implementations in the moving-mesh code AREPO-2. We characterize representative elementary and composite dark-sector models through their particle content, symmetries, interactions, production mechanisms, and constraints. We then establish an explicit mapping from their microscopic properties to the inputs required for structure-formation simulations, including modifications to cosmological initial conditions, internal-state mass splittings and populations, reaction networks, velocity- and angle-dependent cross sections, dissipative energy loss, and decay rates and recoil kinematics. Building on the efficient, scalable SIDM infrastructure introduced in our companion work, we implement isotropic and anisotropic self-scattering with constant or velocity-dependent cross sections, multi-state and inelastic reactions, and dissipative scattering, as well as a dedicated DM decay module. We validate the implementations through beam-lattice deflection experiments, thermalization and uniform-box decay tests, isolated-halo gravothermal core-collapse simulations, and cosmological box and zoom-in simulations. The tests reproduce analytical predictions and published inelastic and dissipative benchmarks, with agreement across numerical schemes. The resulting framework provides a common reference for researchers across disciplines and a practical route from microscopic dark-sector theories to nonlinear astrophysical predictions beyond standard isotropic, elastic SIDM.

entries.title: A Quest for Changing-State AGNs
entries.abstract: We use Gaia Data Release 3 (DR3) light curves to identify photometrically selected changing-state active galactic nucleus (CSAGN) candidates. We employ unsupervised deep learning and anomaly detection methods to identify unusual patterns of variability in the light curves of 872,228 AGNs with known variability. We find that 8,504 light curves show anomalous behavior. Among these, 682 sources show evidence for two-state photometric behavior during the Gaia DR3 observing baseline. These 682 CSAGN candidates were selected using an automated statistical pattern recognition approach based on Gaussian mixture models (GMMs) to identify sources whose magnitude distributions are consistent with two preferred brightness levels, substantially reducing the need for human visual inspection in selecting the CSAGN candidates. The candidates tend to have fainter absolute magnitudes and lower redshifts than the non-anomalous Gaia variable AGN sample, suggesting that some may be accreting at lower rates. Our approach builds a large candidate sample with less reliance on human visual selection. Follow-up observations of these sources can help identify what drives changing-state transitions and clarify their connection to accretion-disk physics and supermassive black hole (SMBH) fueling.

entries.title: An end-to-end experimental pipeline for automated track identification for paleo-detectors
entries.abstract: Paleo-detectors aim to exploit the damage tracks left in natural minerals by cosmic messengers over geological times to reconstruct past fluxes of energetic particles. For cosmic rays, the expected signal is abundant, and the tracks are micron-scale, so they can be revealed by etching and read out with conventional optical microscopy; what remains challenging is turning a bulk sample into a calibrated track-length spectrum that can be quantitatively confronted with theoretical predictions. In this work we present the experimental pipeline we developed for this purpose within the INFN PRImuS experiment, from sample preparation and automated multi-focus microscopy to track recognition with OptimusPrimus, a two-stage machine-learning algorithm, and to a forward-folding model that propagates geometric sectioning, etching and the measured detection response into simulated spectra. The pipeline was built and validated on chemically etched obsidian where the recovered track-length distribution is statistically compatible with expert annotation. In parallel, we developed and characterized a dry argon-plasma etching protocol for halite, an evaporite mineral of particular interest as a low-background cosmic-ray paleo-detector. Since every stage of the pipeline is mineral-agnostic, with only the trained networks and the detection response to be re-derived from annotated data, we are now applying it to plasma-etched halite with the aim of identifying cosmic-ray-induced tracks.

entries.title: Indirect Dark Matter Detection in the Multi-Messenger Era: Experiments, Systematics, Anomalies, and Prospects for Discovery
entries.abstract: Indirect searches for dark matter (DM) span gamma rays, charged cosmic rays, neutrinos, X-rays, radio emission, the cosmic microwave background (CMB), and the 21~cm signal, but reported constraints and anomalies vary in evidential strength. This critical review synthesizes peer-reviewed literature from January 2000 through October 2026 using a structured search strategy. We assess observations through a framework linking particle interactions and halo source terms to propagation or cosmological energy deposition, instrumental response, background modeling, and statistical inference. Fermi-LAT observations of dwarf spheroidal galaxies provide robust GeV-scale benchmarks for DM annihilation, whereas Galactic-center searches offer higher expected signals but depend more on foregrounds and halo profiles. Charged-cosmic-ray measurements are precise but limited by propagation and source uncertainties, while neutrino searches offer complementary sensitivity through solar capture, directional and flavor information, and high-mass annihilation or decay. Several widely discussed signals, including the 3.5~keV line, 511~keV emission, the Galactic-center GeV excess, charged-particle features, cluster radio excesses, and candidate gamma-ray lines remain inconclusive because of limited independent confirmation, uncertain target scaling, spectral degeneracies, or background-modeling limitations. Cosmological observations provide complementary constraints from CMB energy-injection limits and 21~cm measurements of the intergalactic medium. Artificial intelligence increasingly supports reconstruction and inference but requires rigorous calibration and domain-shift validation. The strongest case for DM discovery would require statistically consistent evidence across independent targets, instruments, or messengers, under common particle-physics parameters, and with well-characterized uncertainties.

entries.title: The Cosmic Radio Dipole and Observer Effects in SKA all-sky surveys
entries.abstract: The Square Kilometre Array (SKA) will observe our Universe on the largest scales and so enable the study of fundamental assumptions in cosmology, such as cosmic homogeneity and isotropy. Observations over recent years have reaffirmed an unexpected challenge to the Cosmological Principle first seen in measurements of the cosmic radio dipole. This dipole anisotropy is thought to be caused by our local observer motion, however, it is observed to be about three times larger than predicted, with significances exceeding 5$σ$. The SKA is in a unique position to shed light on this anomaly by measuring this and other effects related to our observer motion. To quantify this, we forecast the capability of large-angle HI and continuum surveys of the SKA to constrain the kinematic matter dipole in galaxy number counts, the modulation of the matter power spectrum by a kinematic dipole, and kinematic spectral distortions of diffuse radio emission.

entries.title: Cosmic Colliders in Binary Blazars Probing Ultra-High-Energy Particle Physics
entries.abstract: While terrestrial colliders and fixed-target cosmic-ray interactions are bounded at center-of-mass (CM) energies $\sqrt{s} \lesssim \mathcal{O}(10^5)\,\text{GeV}$, we demonstrate that bound sub-parsec binary blazars form broad-band, beam-beam hadronic ``Cosmic Colliders'', overcoming such limitation. Driven by modest jet misalignments ($θ_{\rm mis} \sim 1^\circ - 6^\circ$), co-streaming proton beams collide at CM energies reaching $\sqrt{s} \sim 10^{10}\,\text{GeV}$ - six orders of magnitude above the Large Hadron Collider. Operating in a strictly optically thin regime ($τ_{pp} \ll 1$), the system performs a continuous CM energy scan, probing asymptotic QCD scaling, gluon saturation, and Froissart unitarity, while opening a possible high-sensitivity window into physics beyond the Standard Model. Secondary PeV-EeV neutrinos and sub-TeV $γ$-rays fall directly within reach of current and planned observatories such as LHAASO, CTAO, IceCube, and GRAND, establishing binary blazars as laboratories for physics at the ultimate energy limit.

entries.title: R(V) parameter of the dust extinction curve: mapping based on hot stars and connections to diffuse interstellar bands
entries.abstract: Favored carriers of the Diffuse Interstellar Bands (DIBs) are carbonaceous molecules whose constituents have been presumably expelled by dying stars along with those of dust grains. The parallel evolution of DIB carriers and grains and their potential interplay are unknown. We assembled published R(V) measurements of 505 hot stars. We inverted a catalog of extinction data based on Gaia XP spectra and NIR photometry, and used the resulting new 3D extinction map to locate the opaque areas responsible for R(V) for each star. Using archived spectra, we measured their 5780, 5797 and 8620 A DIBs. In parallel, we compared local and line-of-sight (LOS) R(V)s from recent 3D maps with local and LOS Gaia DIB strengths from our recent map. Results: R(V)s from hot stars reveal variations on large spatial scales, confirming with independent data the published 3D pattern. Gaia DIB strength maps show large spatial scale variations similar to those of R(V) maps, with higher abundance of DIB carriers corresponding to higher R(V). LOS Gaia DIB strengths and R(V)s from 3D maps also correlate positively in the R(V) range 2.3-3.4, but there is no connection for higher R(V), likely due to the disappearance of DIB carriers in dense clouds. Despite averaging effects along the LOS to hot stars, we find differences in R(V)-DIB relationships among the three DIBs, with an evolution from negative to positive correlation from the zeta- to the sigma-type DIBs. This can be understood in the frame of the bimodal evolution of R(V) with the extinction, with the zeta (resp. sigma) DIB carrier disappearance in the decreasing (resp. increasing) phase of R(V). Various combinations of DIB strengths and DIB ratios may allow to define the range of R(V), but the relationship between DIBs and R(V) also appears to depend on the wavelength range used to determine R(V).

entries.title: Extinction by non-spherical particles with the Nanoparticle Transition Matrix Code: perspectives for interstellar medium and exoplanetary atmospheres
entries.abstract: The Transition Matrix formalism (T-matrix) offers an optimal solution to the problem of radiation scattering and absorption by particles characterized by a high degree of chemical and structural complexity. However, its application to particle models composed by large numbers of constituents has been classically limited by the substantial computational burden of the method. As a consequence, the investigation of light scattering and absorption processes, in cases where particle asymmetry and non-homogeneity play an important role, typically need to rely on simplifying assumptions which affect the correct interpretation of transmission spectra and extinction curves. This problem has a huge impact on many fields of scientific application. In particular, it has a critical role in astrophysics, because the ability to model highly non homogeneous particles is a fundamental requirement to understand the role of extinction in different phases of the interstellar medium (ISM), as well as to probe the physics of light transmission in planetary atmospheres within the Solar System and beyond. In this work we describe the application of a new implementation of the T-matrix formalism, based on the framework originally developed by Borghese, Denti & Saija and named Nano-particle Transition Matrix code, which leverages the power of modern hardware architectures to reduce the computational costs related to the solution of relevant particle models for the investigation of dust in the ISM and of hot-Jupyter class planets atmospheric aerosols. This new implementation of the T-matrix formalism can handle calculations of increasing complexity with a direct impact in the interpretation of the transmission spectra of transiting exoplanets produced by the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) and of those expected from the Atmospheric Remote-sensing Infrared Exoplanet Large survey (ARIEL).

entries.title: JWST Imaging of Edge-on Protoplanetary Disks. V. Flux Ratio Reversal and Disk-edge Structure in the Flying Saucer
entries.abstract: We present near- and mid-infrared broadband imaging observations of the edge-on protoplanetary disk 2MASS J16281370-2431391, a.k.a. the 'Flying Saucer', obtained with NIRCam and MIRI on board JWST. These data are combined with archival optical and near-IR broadband imaging from HST, millimeter dust continuum emission from ALMA, and optical lightcurves from the K2 and TESS for a comprehensive multi-wavelength study. The JWST observations reveal a reversal of the flux ratio between the two reflection nebulae at near-infrared wavelengths (2-3 $μm$), which can be explained by a misaligned inner disk. For the first time, JWST reveals the bright lining along the disk edge at 2 and 3 $μm$, arising from forward scattering of background photons by dust grains near the $τ\approx 1$ layer. By combining the dust lane thickness measured with HST and JWST, we find the dust grains up to at least $\sim$3$μ$m are vertically mixed throughout the disk and have undergone significant growth. In addition, comparison of earlier HST/NICMOS J and K band images with those from JWST/NIRCam reveals variability in the scattered-light morphology, as well as measurable proper motion of the system with respect to the background stars, confirming that the Flying Saucer is co-moving with the young star population of $ρ$ Ophiuchi.

entries.title: The nearby Type II supernova 2024ggi beyond 600 days: circumstellar interaction and dust formation
entries.abstract: The Type II SN 2024ggi is one of the nearest core-collapse SNe to have exploded in recent decades. Its proximity has enabled extensive multiwavelength monitoring from early times through the nebular phase. Signatures of late-time interaction between the SN ejecta and hydrogen-rich circumstellar material (CSM) have recently been reported. Here we extend its study using late-time optical photometry and spectroscopy from 570 to 820 d after explosion. We investigate the emergence and evolution of late-time ejecta-CSM interaction and constrain the geometry of the interaction region and the properties of newly formed dust. Comparisons with other interacting SNe II and with synthetic spectra are presented. We model the H$α$ profile with the Monte Carlo radiative-transfer code Damocles, including both gas and dust components. Spectroscopic signatures of interaction precede the photometric flattening. The spectra evolve from ejecta-dominated to interaction-dominated as H$α$ develops a broad, boxy profile. The optical light curves subsequently flatten relative to the $^{56}$Co decay rate at approximately 650-670 d. The emission lines show a systematic blue-to-red asymmetry that requires a dust component newly formed within the ejecta. The inferred dust mass formed in the ejecta is $10^{-6}-10^{-5}$ M$_\odot$ if the grains are amorphous carbon or a carbon-silicate mixture, but can reach up to $10^{-3}$ M$_\odot$ for pure silicates.

entries.title: Vanishing Love Numbers of Kerr-Newman Black Holes
entries.abstract: Tidal Love numbers characterize the conservative response of compact objects to external perturbations and provide a powerful probe of their nature. While the static Love numbers of Schwarzschild, Kerr, and Reissner--Nordström black holes remarkably vanish, the tidal response of a generic Kerr--Newman black hole has remained unexplored due to the intrinsic coupling between gravitational and electromagnetic perturbations. Exploiting a recent breakthrough in the separability of these perturbations, we analytically determine the static tidal response of the most general stationary black hole in four-dimensional Einstein--Maxwell theory. For arbitrary multipole order, charge, and spin, we show that the entire matrix of conservative Love numbers vanishes, including the mixed gravito-electromagnetic couplings. We also compute the nonvanishing static dissipative response induced by frame dragging.

entries.title: Interpreting the stacked kinetic SZ signal II: the degeneracy between satellite galaxies and baryonic feedback
entries.abstract: The kinetic Sunyaev-Zel'dovich (kSZ) signal stacked around a galaxy sample traces the gas around halos and is a powerful probe of baryonic feedback. Its interpretation, however, depends on the satellite galaxies in the sample. Using the FLAMINGO hydrodynamical simulations and DESI-like samples of luminous red galaxies (LRGs), bright galaxies survey (BGS), and emission-line galaxies (ELGs), we show that satellites and feedback have similar effects: both suppress the small-scale signal. This degeneracy arises because stacking on satellites, which are offset from the centre of their host haloes, mimics the extended gas distribution produced by feedback. Although satellites make up only 20-30% of each sample, they account for 50-80% of the signal because they occupy more massive halos than centrals; thus their imprint on the stacked profiles can be as large as that of feedback. At the precision of current DESI$\times$ACT data, neglecting satellites in the modelling biases the inferred gas fractions low, by up to a factor of two, and overestimates the feedback strength, particularly for the LRG and BGS samples. Remaining agnostic about the satellite population avoids this bias but reduces the constraining power, so robust constraints would require knowing the satellite fraction to better than 10%, for instance from lensing and clustering data of the same galaxy samples. Finally, a further contribution from satellites will become statistically significant with upcoming surveys: satellites trace the anisotropic gas distribution around their host haloes, an effect that contributes 10% of the signal, and will likely require simulation-based models to capture.

analysis.result: 对10个黑洞X射线双星共34次IXPE观测进行了偏振时变搜索。软态源 4U 1630–47 探测到了显著的偏振度线性上升，变化斜率为 $(3.25 \pm 0.66) \times 10^{-5}\,\mathrm{ks}^{-1}$（偏振度 PD 在 $844\,\mathrm{ks}$ 时间内从 $6.6\%$ 升至 $9.4\%$，显著度达 $4.9\sigma$），且偏振角保持恒定。对未显著探测到时变的强偏振源，利用功率约束上限（PCL）给出 $99\%$ CL 限制：bin-to-bin 的 PD 均方根（RMS）上限在 $<12.8\%$ 至 $\sim 100\%$ 之间，偏振角 RMS 游走上限限制在 $<2.9^\circ$ 至 $30^\circ$（基于旋转 Stokes 参数关系 $\delta u' \approx 2\,\mathrm{PD}\,\delta\psi$）。
analysis.problem: 致密天体黑洞X射线双星的吸积流/冕几何在高能波段的瞬态演化与偏振时变缺乏系统性统计约束；同时，X射线偏振数据（如IXPE）处理繁复且多重假设检验繁多，利用大模型智能体进行端到端自动化天文分析时存在幻觉、捷径计算与统计陷阱。
analysis.method: 利用LangGraph/MCP解耦构建双智能体（Claude/Gemini）项目生成、执行引擎与溯源审计器；采用PCUBE提取Stokes参数，旋转坐标系至对齐均值偏振方向 $q'=q\cos 2\bar{\psi}+u\sin 2\bar{\psi}$ 和 $u'=-q\sin 2\bar{\psi}+u\cos 2\bar{\psi}$；通过加权拟合 $\chi^2=\sum_{i}(x_{i}-c)^{2}/\sigma_{i}^{2}$ 与多重检验校正（Bonferroni和BH法），并计算功率约束上限 $a_{\rm PCL}=\max(a_{99}, a_{99}^{\rm med})$，其中 $P[\chi^{2}(a_{99}) \le \chi^2_{\rm obs}]=0.01$。
assumptions: 在旋转偏振参考系中假定小偏振角变动下满足线性近似 $\delta u' \approx 2\,\mathrm{PD}\,\delta\psi$

analysis.result: 通过VLTI/GRAVITY干涉拟合得出WR 6的连续谱均匀圆盘直径为 $0.37\text{--}0.48\ {\rm mas}$（对应距离 $1.4\ {\rm kpc}$ 下的辐射半径 $\approx 60\ R_\odot$），排除了早于B2.5 V（$M \approx 6\ M_\odot$）的主序伴星；首次在风中直接干涉探测到1至3个偏心大尺度密度结构，视向速度分布在 $-1589\pm 28\ {\rm km\ s^{-1}}$ 至 $+918\pm 14\ {\rm km\ s^{-1}}$ 之间（对比恒星终极风速 $v_\infty = 1759\ {\rm km\ s^{-1}}$），其多结构分布与时间演化直接支持了多重CIRs物理图景并排除了单伴星假说。
analysis.problem: WR 6中存在的 $P = 3.76\ {\rm d}$ 周期性光度、偏振与谱线轮廓变化长期存在争议，即究竟源自大质量恒星自转调制的共转相互作用区（CIRs）还是致密/低质量伴星的轨道调制，此前缺乏直接的空间角分辨观测判定。
analysis.method: 利用VLTI/GRAVITY长基线红外干涉仪（基线达 $202\ {\rm m}$，K波段分辨率 $\sim 1\ {\rm mas}$，$R \sim 4\,134$）开展6个历元的干涉观测，联合地基高分辨率光谱（NRES与eShel），使用PMOIRED中的嵌套采样（nested sampling）算法全局搜索参数空间，将谱线差分相位（DP）解耦为偏心发射结构，并结合视线几何关系 $\Delta Z = \frac{\sqrt{\Delta E^2 + \Delta N^2}}{\arctan \theta}$（其中天顶角 $\theta = \arccos\left[\frac{\lambda - \lambda_0}{\lambda_0} \frac{c}{v_\infty}\right]$）构建平流三维构型。

analysis.result: 研究得到核心物理标度律与统计分布：(1) 等待时间 $\Delta t$ 展现双组分结构，在 $\Delta t \lesssim 2~{\rm s}$ 为单次活跃幕内雪崩驱动的指数分布，而在 $\Delta t > 2~{\rm s}$ 服从左帕累托对数正态（lPln）分布，长尾幂律为 $P(\Delta t) \propto \Delta t^{-0.64}$（帕累托指数 $\alpha_{\rm l} = 0.36\pm 0.04$）；(2) 发射测度代用指标 $\tilde{\rm EM} = K (k_{\rm B}T)^{1/2}$ 与温度 $T$ 呈双分支结构，上升支斜率 $b_{\rm rise} = 1.78\pm 0.23$（与磁环固定尺度加热模型 ${\rm EM} \propto T^{8/3}$ 接近），下降支斜率 $b_{\rm fall} = -0.71\pm 0.21$ 由体积膨胀主导；(3) 能量释放标度 $S_{\gamma} = F E_{\rm c}^{-\gamma}$ 联合拟合给出 $\gamma = 0.94\pm 0.29$（与光子数通量标度 $\gamma=1$ 一致，显著排斥理想黑体辐射面积标度 $\gamma \approx 4$），高能端幂律尾指数 $\alpha_S = 2.15\pm 0.13$；(4) 能通量遵循阈值幂律 $P(F) \propto (F+F_{0})^{-\alpha_{F}}$，高通量斜率 $\alpha_{F} = 2.23\pm 0.10$（阈值 $F_{0}=7.9\times 10^{-7}~{\rm erg~cm^{-2}~s^{-1}}$），支持磁层磁重联自组织临界态。
analysis.problem: 磁星 X 射线爆发内部子结构（MXFs）的物理本质、时间聚类规律、热力学演化机制，以及其究竟起源于磁层磁重联雪崩还是星壳破裂能量释放，及其与 FRB 的级联对应机制。

analysis.result: 在 17 年 Fermi-LAT 数据中，该源能谱在单对数抛物线连续谱之上表现出显著的高斯谱超出：最佳拟合中心能量 $E_{\mathrm{signal}} = 13.07 \pm 2.25\,\mathrm{GeV}$，线性高斯宽度 $\sigma_{\mathrm{signal}} = 10.00 \pm 0.02\,\mathrm{GeV}$，对数空间谱峰能量 $E_{\mathrm{peak}} = 19.26 \pm 1.52\,\mathrm{GeV}$，积分光子通量 $F_{\mathrm{signal}} = (3.62 \pm 0.72) \times 10^{-10}\,\mathrm{ph\,cm^{-2}\,s^{-1}}$，检验统计量 $\mathrm{TS} = 39.79$（显著性约 $5.7\sigma$）。时变分析表明前 8.5 年通量为 $(4.59 \times 10^{-10}\,\mathrm{ph\,cm^{-2}\,s^{-1}})$，后 8.5 年降至 $(2.67 \times 10^{-10}\,\mathrm{ph\,cm^{-2}\,s^{-1}})$，表现出明显的暂态特性。
analysis.problem: 标准相对论喷流模型难以在不精细调节参数的情况下产生孤立且具有时变性的 $\sim 19\,\mathrm{GeV}$ 宽能谱隆起，且模型参数的微调易导致中微子或未被观测证实的低能辐射超额。
analysis.method: 利用 Fermi-LAT 约 17 年 Pass 8 数据（100 MeV–1 TeV），采用单对数抛物线连续谱模型 $\frac{dN}{dE} = K(E/E_{0})^{-\alpha - \beta \ln(E/E_{0})}$ 作为零假设，对比叠加线性高斯谱分量 $N_{\mathrm{signal}}(E) = \frac{N_{0}}{\sigma_{\mathrm{signal}}\sqrt{2\pi}} \exp\left[-\frac{(E - E_{\mathrm{signal}})^{2}}{2\sigma_{\mathrm{signal}}^{2}}\right]$ 的极大似然拟合，并进行了 IRF 体系、能量色散与银河弥散背景缩放 $\pm 10\%$ 的系统误差稳健性测试。

analysis.result: 测定 J0010$-$1735 的金属丰度为 $\mathrm{[Fe/H]} = -2.22 \pm 0.11$（LTE），并呈现极强的快中子俘获过程增强 $\mathrm{[Eu/Fe]} = +1.30$ 以及 $\mathrm{[Ba/Eu]} = -0.45$；铁峰元素显著匮乏（如 $\mathrm{[Mn\,I/Fe]} = -0.77$、$\mathrm{[Ni/Fe]} = -0.48$），与前身星质量约为 $0.88\text{--}0.97\,M_\odot$ 的亚钱德拉塞卡质量（$\mathrm{sub}\text{-}M_{\mathrm{Ch}}$）Type Ia 超新星模型产额一致；钙丰度异常偏高（$\mathrm{[Ca/Fe]} = +0.17$），提示富钙快变源（Ca-rich gap transient）贡献；利用核宇宙年代学公式 $\tau = 46.7\,\mathrm{Gyr}\,[\log(\mathrm{Th/X})_0 - \log(\mathrm{Th/X})_*]$ 结合实测 $\log\epsilon(\mathrm{Th/Eu}) = -0.26 \pm 0.24$ 导出恒星年龄为 $\tau = 12.5 \pm 4.2\;\mathrm{Gyr}$。
analysis.problem: 极贫金属吸积银晕星中异常元素模式（轻元素、$\alpha$ 元素与铁峰元素低丰度，但伴随 Ca 异常偏高与极端 $r$-过程强增丰）的核合成起源与母体矮星系性质尚不明确。
analysis.method: 利用 Magellan/MIKE 高分辨率阶梯光栅光谱（$R \sim 50,000\text{--}60,000$），基于 1D LTE（结合 ATLAS-Kurucz 模型与 MOOG）及 1D NLTE（LOTUS、Turbospectrum/TSFitPy）进行恒星大气参数与 45 种元素丰度精确测定，并通过 Gaia 结合银河系动力学势积分与 Toomre 图进行轨道动力学溯源分析。
assumptions: 中子俘获元素生成以快中子俘获过程（$r$-process）为主导，放射性定年假设高熵风（HEW）产额比作为初始放射性同位素比例 $\log(\mathrm{Th/Eu})_0$。

analysis.result: 通过单云近似与局部最优发射云（LOC）光电离模型分析发现，亚爱丁顿吸积源中由响应度反演的 BLR 入射电离光子通量 $\Phi_{\mathrm{H}}^{\mathrm{ion}}$ 与各向同性假设通量 $\Phi_{\mathrm{H}}^{\mathrm{iso}}$ 吻合良好，投影因子仅为 $\cos\theta_{\mathrm{obs}}/\cos\theta_{\mathrm{BLR}} \sim 1\text{–}3.3$（$\sim 0\text{–}0.5\;\mathrm{dex}$）；但在超爱丁顿吸积体系（$\dot{\mathcal{M}} \ge 3$）中，细盘（slim disk）中心鼓起产生强烈的自遮蔽（self-shadowing）效应，使得照射到宽线区的通量显著降低，达到 $\Phi_{\mathrm{H}}^{\mathrm{ion}} \sim 0.001\text{–}0.15\,\Phi_{\mathrm{H}}^{\mathrm{iso}}$（差异达 $1.5\text{–}3$ 个数量级），成功解释了超爱丁顿 AGN 中 BLR 尺度和 $\mathrm{H}\beta$ 等效宽度系统性偏小的现象。

analysis.result: 若双中子星并合（NSMs）是唯一的 r-过程源，其最小延迟时间必须缩短至 $t_{\mathrm{min,NSM}} = 14\text{--}16\ \mathrm{Myr}$（Fornax 星系中甚至达 $11_{-1}^{+2}\ \mathrm{Myr}$），这与双星演化及引力辐射吸积时延理论相冲突，强烈支持早期存在快 r-过程源（如磁转动超新星 MRSNe）；同时，理论 NSM 产额必须对轻 r-过程元素进行下调，Sr 和 Y 需分别减少约 5 倍和 50 倍（$\mathrm{normSr_{NSM}} \approx 0.2$, $\mathrm{normY_{NSM}} \approx 0.02$）。对于 Ia 型超新星，其最小时延拟合限制在 $t_{\mathrm{min,Ia}} \approx 50\text{--}100\ \mathrm{Myr}$。
analysis.problem: 双中子星并合（NSM）的时延分布（DTD）较长，能否作为早期金属贫瘠矮星系中 r-过程元素的唯一产生渠道，还是必须依赖大质量恒星核心坍缩驱动的快源（prompt r-process source，如 MRSNe）。
analysis.method: 构建包含吸积、外流与恒星形成的单区瞬时混合星系化学演化（GCE）开箱模型，结合 MCMC（`emcee`）在 9 维丰度空间与金属度分布函数（MDF）上拟合观测数据（引入测量上限 CDF 惩罚）。NSM 与 SNeIa 的 DTD 分别采用幂律标度 $\Psi_{\mathrm{NSM}} \propto t^{-1.5}$ 与 $\Psi_{\mathrm{Ia}} \propto t^{-1.1}$，核心演化控制方程为 $\xi_j(t) = \int_0^t (\dot{\xi}_{j,\mathrm{II}} + \dot{\xi}_{j,\mathrm{AGB}} + \dot{\xi}_{j,\mathrm{Ia}} + \dot{\xi}_{j,r} - \dot{\xi}_{j,\mathrm{SF}} + \dot{\xi}_{j,\mathrm{in}} - \dot{\xi}_{j,\mathrm{out}}) dt$。

analysis.reason: 该工作利用 Chandra X 射线观测超新星遗迹 RX J1713.7−3946 前激波上游的热点分布，首次直接测定了宇宙线质子的扩散尺度并约束了激波上游磁场放大强度，为超新星激波与周星介质相互作用中的粒子加速极限（PeVatron 判定）提供了关键观测判据。
analysis.result:
通过激波前锋外 X 射线热点的径向分布，测得高能质子的特征扩散长度为 $l_{\mathrm{diff}} \sim 1~\mathrm{pc}$。在假定粒子束缚达到玻姆极限（回旋因子 $\eta = 1$）条件下，基于次级电子同步辐射模型推导出激波上游磁场强度为 $B_{\mathrm{up}} \sim 10~\mu\mathrm{G}$：
$$B_{\mathrm{up}} = 14\eta \left( rac{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{sync}}}{1~\mathrm{keV}}ight)^{1/2} \left( rac{B_{\mathrm{clump}}}{1~\mathrm{mG}}ight)^{-1/2} \left( rac{V_{\mathrm{sh}}}{3000~\mathrm{km~s^{-1}}}ight)^{-1} \left( rac{l_{\mathrm{diff}}}{1~\mathrm{pc}}ight)^{-1}~\mu\mathrm{G}$$
结合遗迹年龄 $t_{\mathrm{age}} \sim 1600	ext{--}2000~\mathrm{yr}$ 与激波速度 $V_{\mathrm{sh}} \sim 3000~\mathrm{km~s^{-1}}$，受限的最大质子能量为：
$$E_{\mathrm{max}} = 96\eta^{-1} \left( rac{B_{\mathrm{up}}}{14~\mu\mathrm{G}}ight) \left( rac{V_{\mathrm{sh}}}{3000~\mathrm{km~s^{-1}}}ight)^2 \left( rac{t_{\mathrm{age}}}{1600~\mathrm{yr}}ight)~\mathrm{TeV} \sim 100~\mathrm{TeV}$$
表明当前上游磁场放大不足以将粒子加速到 $\sim 1~\mathrm{PeV}$，独立解释了该 SNR 在 TeV 伽马射线能谱中观测到的截断现象。
analysis.problem: 超新星遗迹激波被视为银河系 PeV 能区宇宙线（膝区）的主要加速候选体，但要实现 PeV 加速需要激波上游区产生强烈的非共振 Bell 不稳定性磁场放大以有效束缚最高能量粒子；然而，激波上游区域的磁场放大强度长期缺乏直接观测约束。
analysis.method: 利用 Chandra ACIS 档案数据，采用 CIAO `wavdetect` 工具及 Li & Ma 公式筛选显著度 $S > 3\sigma$ 的 X 射线点状热点（hotspots）；在 XSPEC 中对源区与邻近背景区建立包含吸收幂律（`TBabs * pegpwrlw`）及非 X 射线背景（NXB）的联合拟合模型；结合激波上游分子云块中的 $pp$ 强子相互作用模型（$\pi^\pm \to \mu^\pm \to e^\pm$ 次级轻子能量关系 $E_e \sim E_p / 20$，同步辐射特征能量 $E_e = 7(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{sync}}/1~\mathrm{keV})^{1/2} (B_{\mathrm{clump}}/1~\mathrm{mG})^{-1/2}~\mathrm{TeV}$）以及扩散长度模型 $l_{\mathrm{diff}} = \kappa / V_{\mathrm{sh}} = 0.1\eta (E_p/10~\mathrm{TeV}) (B_{\mathrm{up}}/10~\mu\mathrm{G})^{-1} (V_{\mathrm{sh}}/3000~\mathrm{km~s^{-1}})^{-1}~\mathrm{pc}$，从热点面密度衰减尺度反解 $B_{\mathrm{up}}$。
assumptions: 假设激波上游的 X 射线热点是由扩散进入前激波未扰动区域的高能质子与前身星风扫过后残留的致密分子云块发生强子相互作用（pp 碰撞）产生的次级电子/正电子发射同步辐射所致。
反推上游磁场强度时假设上游磁场空间分布均匀（推导出的 $B_{\mathrm{up}}$ 对应空间平均值），且分子云块内部磁场符合基于气体密度的经验标度关系取为 $B_{\mathrm{clump}} = 1~\mathrm{mG}$（对应 $n_{\mathrm{clump}} = 10^6~\mathrm{cm^{-3}}$）。
limits: H.E.S.S. 的点扩散函数（PSF）角分辨率有限，无法在激波前锋处精细剥离上游和下游的 TeV 伽马射线发射，导致上游 $F_{\mathrm{X}}/F_\gamma \sim 0.1$ 的通量比值为粗略估计。
上游磁场空间结构可能随离激波前锋的距离增大而衰减，回旋因子 $\eta$ 也可能随距离增加，观测推导值受限于空间平均假定。
无法完全排除上游热点来源于激波前锋加速的原初轻子（电子）直接扩散的可能（但在该轻子假说下推导出的 $B_{\mathrm{up}} \sim 0.7~\mu\mathrm{G}$ 同样无法加速质子到 PeV）。

analysis.result: SLSNe II 的近紫外超额光度与总拟热光度维持恒定比值（$L_{\rm ex}/L_{\rm bol} \approx 0.01\text{--}0.1$）。假设紫外超额由星周相互作用（CSI）主导驱动，利用标度关系 $\frac{dM}{dt} = \frac{2L_{\rm ex}}{\epsilon} v_{\rm CSM} v_{\rm sh}^{-3}$（取辐射效率 $\epsilon = 0.5$，$v_{\rm CSM} = 100\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$），推断前身星爆发前数年至数十年的质量损失率下限为 $\dot{M} \sim 10^{-4}\text{--}0.03\,\mathrm{M_\odot\,yr^{-1}}$；若相互作用主导总光度，则实际 $\dot{M} \sim 0.2\text{--}0.3\,\mathrm{M_\odot\,yr^{-1}}$。SN 2008es 类子样本总辐射能量达 $(1\text{--}3)\times 10^{51}\,\mathrm{erg}$，且低几何填充因子（$f \sim 0.1$）排除了纯中微子驱动激波转换机制，必须由中心引擎驱动。

analysis.result: 多波段测光显示光变曲线在 $600\sim 650\ \mathrm{d}$ 发生变平（flattening），脱离了 $^{56}\mathrm{Co} \to {}^{56}\mathrm{Fe}$ 的放射性衰变率；光谱在 $706\ \mathrm{d}$ 与 $811\ \mathrm{d}$ 展现出延伸至 $v \approx \pm 8000\ \mathrm{km\ s^{-1}}$ 的盒状（boxy）H$\alpha$ 轮廓，红翼明显受抑；辐射转移模拟测得冷致密壳层（CDS）几何厚度比为 $R_{\rm in}/R_{\rm out} \simeq 0.7$，形成的新生尘埃质量为 $M_{\rm dust} \sim 5\times 10^{-6}\text{--}5\times 10^{-5}\ M_\odot$（碳质或碳-硅酸盐混合）或 $\sim 10^{-3}\ M_\odot$（纯硅酸盐），扫过的 CSM 位于 $r \sim (4\text{--}7)\times 10^{16}\ \mathrm{cm}$，对应爆发前 $\sim 10^3\ \mathrm{yr}$ 的恒星风物质。

opening_brief.worth_knowing_summary: 通过 Fe K 边 XAFS 分析，确定铁原子在各组分中的分配为：约 $38\%$ 为金属铁，约 $47\%$ 赋存于铁硫化物，其余赋存于硅酸盐。；一个处于逆行轨道（倾角 $\theta_{\bullet}=150^{\circ}$、初始 $a_{\bullet}=0.15\text{ pc}$、质量 $m_{\bullet}=2000\,{\rm M}_{\odot}$）的 IMBH 能够在活星团中约 $5\text{ Myr}$ 内将恒星盘瓦解为三个类似盘的子结构及角动量纤维结构；IMBH 轨道因 Chandrasekhar 动力学摩擦（库仑对数需折半 $\ln\Lambda = \frac{1}{2}\ln(M/m_{\bullet})$）在 $10\text{ Myr}$ 内半长轴衰减超过 $50\%$；内区（$a\le 0.04\text{ pc}$）偏心率加热由星团双体弛豫主导，但观测中极高偏心率（$e \sim 0.97$）可通过 Hills 机制双星潮汐瓦解形成，捕获星轨道满足 $1/a_{\mathrm{cap}} = 1/a + 1/a_{\mathrm{cap,0}}$（其中 $a_{\mathrm{cap,0}} = (a_{\mathrm{b}}/\sqrt{2})(M/m_{\mathrm{b}})^{2/3}$）。 等。
